scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a configuration change window on router2, pc1 (195.11.14.2)
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach pc1. Both
routers are up, and the two ends of the inter-AS link still ping
each other directly (193.10.11.1 <-> 193.10.11.2), but the eBGP
session between router1 and router2 will not come up. Investigate.

injection.action: set a wrong remote-as (65001 instead of 1) on router2's neighbor statement for router1

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 BGP configuration (neighbor remote-as)
Mechanism: router2's config now says `neighbor 193.10.11.1
  remote-as 65001`, but router1 really is AS 1. During session
  setup router1's OPEN message carries AS 1; router2 compares it
  against the configured 65001, rejects the OPEN (bad peer AS
  notification), and the session never reaches Established. With
  no session, no prefixes are exchanged: router1 never learns
  200.1.1.0/24 and router2 never learns 195.11.14.0/24, so pc1 and
  pc2 cannot reach each other. The underlying link is healthy
  (direct pings across 193.10.11.0/24 work) and both daemons run.
Localization: router2
Root cause: wrong remote-as (65001 instead of 1) on router2's
  neighbor statement for 193.10.11.1
Fix: restore remote-as 1 on router2 (see [FIX])
scenario.fix_spec:
Restore the correct peer AS on router2:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 2" -c "no neighbor 193.10.11.1" -c "neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1"`
The eBGP session establishes and the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged.
(A `service frr restart` on router2 also restores it, since /etc/frr/frr.conf
on disk was never modified.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: FRR BGP configuration on router2 (bgpd neighbor stanza for the inter-AS link on eth0).

Mechanism: The eBGP session tears down during the OPEN exchange because the peer AS numbers do not match. When router1 (AS 1) sends an OPEN, router2 is configured to expect a peer in AS 65001, so it rejects the session and sends a BGP Notification “OPEN Message Error/Bad Peer AS,” leaving the session in Idle. With eBGP down, neither router learns the other’s LAN prefix, so pc1 and pc2 cannot reach each other even though the inter-router link still pings.

Localization: On router2, bgpd shows neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 65001, while router1 is configured as AS 1 with neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2. Evidence: “show bgp neighbor 193.10.11.1” on router2 reports “Last reset … Notification sent (OPEN Message Error/Bad Peer AS)” and state Idle; “show ip bgp summary” on both routers shows the session never comes up.

Root cause: Misconfigured remote-as on router2 (set to 65001 instead of 1) introduced during the change window.

Corrective fix: On router2, correct the neighbor to match router1’s AS: under router bgp 2, configure “no neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 65001” followed by “neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1” and clear the session if needed. The eBGP peering should establish and routes 195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24 will be exchanged, restoring pc1↔pc2 connectivity.

per_axis.rationale: The submission explicitly localizes the fault to router2, repeatedly stating the misconfigured neighbor and showing router2-specific outputs and fixes.

The agent prescribes removing the wrong remote-as and configuring neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1 on router2 (or clearing/restarting), which matches the expected fix.
